title: Chrysler 300 Engines by Year (1955–2023)
description: Every factory engine in the Chrysler 300 by year: letter-car Hemis and wedges, the 440 TNT, the 300M's 3.5 V6, and the Hemi and SRT V8s of the 300C.
intro: The Chrysler 300 began as the 1955 C-300, the first of the letter-series cars that ran to the 1965 300L. A non-letter 300 sport series ran alongside from 1962 to 1971; the name returned for 1979, as the 300M from 1999 to 2004, and as the rear-drive 300 from 2005 to 2023.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: Letter series (C-300 to 300L)
intro: The 331 and 354 FirePower Hemis, the 392 Hemi, then the 413 wedge with long or short cross-ram induction. There was no 300I.

generations.name: 300 sport series
intro: The 383 and 413 wedges, then the 440 and the 440 TNT, including the 1970 300-H.
A Cordoba-based coupe with the 360 four-barrel.

generations.name: 300M
intro: The 3.5 SOHC V6, uprated for the 300M Special.

generations.name: 300 and 300C (LX)
intro: The 2.7 and 3.5 V6s, the 5.7 Hemi in the 300C and the 6.1 Hemi in the SRT8.

generations.name: 300 and 300C (LD)
intro: The 3.6 Pentastar V6, the 5.7 Hemi, the 6.4 in the 2012–2014 SRT8 and the 2023 300C.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
